quickAnswers.question: When can I check in for my Southwest flight?
quickAnswers.answer: Online and app check-in opens 24 hours before scheduled departure. Arrive early on day of travel for bag drop and security.

quickAnswers.question: Do Southwest flights have assigned seats?
quickAnswers.answer: Yes — all Southwest flights now feature assigned seating. Choose seats when you book or manage your trip later.

quickAnswers.question: How many bags can I check for free?
quickAnswers.answer: Southwest's baggage policy allows two free checked bags (size/weight limits apply) plus carryons that fit under the seat or in the overhead bin.

learning.title: How do I check in for my flight?
learning.subtitle: Online and app check-in opens 24 hours before departure.
learning.summary: Check in on Southwest.com or the app starting 24 hours before your flight, then get your boarding pass and head to the airport.
learning.content:
How do I check in for my flight?

Online check-in opens 24 hours before your scheduled departure.

What to do first
Open My Trips on Southwest.com or the Southwest app, select your flight, and follow check-in prompts for each passenger.

Boarding pass options
Save a mobile pass, print at home, or use an airport kiosk or ticket counter.

When to escalate
If check-in is blocked or your name does not match travel documents, contact Southwest support before you leave for the airport.

learning.title: Assigned seats on Southwest
learning.subtitle: All Southwest flights now feature assigned seating.
learning.summary: Choose your seat when booking or later in Manage Reservation. Seat options and fees depend on fare product.
learning.content:
Assigned seats on Southwest

Southwest now assigns seats on every flight.

What to do first
During booking, pick seats for each passenger or continue with available seats and change them later in Manage Reservation.

Fare tip
Wanna Get Away®, Wanna Get Away Plus®, Anytime, and Business Select® include different seat selection windows and benefits.

When to escalate
If you need accessible seating, start with Disability-Related Accommodations before your travel day.

learning.title: Baggage allowance and fees
learning.subtitle: Carryon and checked bag rules for Southwest Customers.
learning.summary: Southwest allows two free checked bags within size and weight limits, plus personal item and carryon guidelines.
learning.content:
Baggage allowance and fees

Know what you can bring before you pack.

What to do first
Review carryon size limits and the two free checked bags policy on your trip confirmation.

Special items
Sporting equipment and oversized items may have extra rules or fees.

When to escalate
Report delayed or damaged bags at the airport baggage office, then track the claim online.

learning.title: Change or cancel my reservation
learning.subtitle: Same-day changes, cancellations, and travel funds.
learning.summary: Most fares can be changed or canceled online. Value remaining is often held as travel funds based on your fare type.
learning.content:
Change or cancel my reservation

Use Manage Reservation to update your trip.

What to do first
Find your confirmation, then choose Change or Cancel and follow fare rules shown for each passenger.

Same-day options
Same-day confirmed changes and standby may be available depending on fare and seat inventory.

When to escalate
If your flight was canceled by Southwest, review rebooking and refund options under Delays & Cancellations.

learning.title: Rapid Rewards points and A-List
learning.subtitle: Earn points, track tiers, and use Companion Pass.
learning.summary: Rapid Rewards members earn points on flights and partners. A-List and Companion Pass have annual qualifying thresholds.
learning.content:
Rapid Rewards points and A-List

Manage loyalty benefits in your Rapid Rewards account.

What to do first
Sign in to view points balance, tier progress, and Companion Pass status.

Missing points
Request credit for a past flight from Rapid Rewards account activity if points did not post.

When to escalate
For locked accounts or profile name changes, use the Rapid Rewards account update forms in Help Center.

learning.title: What if my flight is delayed or canceled?
learning.subtitle: Rebooking, notifications, and irregular operations help.
learning.summary: Southwest will notify you of schedule changes. Rebook in the app or with an agent, and review voucher or refund options when eligible.
learning.content:
What if my flight is delayed or canceled?

Stay flexible when irregular operations happen.

What to do first
Check your trip status in the app and accept a rebooked itinerary if offered.

Customer options
Depending on the disruption, you may rebook, cancel for funds, or request additional help at the ticket counter.

When to escalate
For overnight disruptions or expense reimbursement, follow the Help Center request forms for vouchers or compensation.

learning.title: How do I use travel funds?
learning.subtitle: Apply unused funds to a future Southwest reservation.
learning.summary: Travel funds from eligible canceled trips can be applied at booking. Check expiration dates in your account.
learning.content:
How do I use travel funds?

Travel funds stay attached to the passenger named on the original ticket unless rules say otherwise.

What to do first
Sign in, open travel funds, and note the amount and expiration before you book.

At checkout
Apply funds on Southwest.com or in the app when paying for a new reservation.

When to escalate
If funds are missing or expired early, contact support with your original confirmation number.

learning.title: Disability-related accommodations
learning.subtitle: Wheelchair assistance, service animals, and seating needs.
learning.summary: Request airport assistance and accessible seating ahead of travel so Southwest can prepare for your trip.
learning.content:
Disability-related accommodations

Southwest can support a range of accessible travel needs.

What to do first
Add assistance requests when you book or through Manage Reservation before departure day.

Airport arrival
Allow extra time for assistance at check-in, security, and boarding.

When to escalate
If you need to discuss medical seating or service animal documentation, contact the accessibility support team before you fly.

messages.content: How do I check in for my flight?

Online and app check-in opens 24 hours before your scheduled departure.

1. Open My Trips on Southwest.com or in the Southwest app.
2. Select your flight and follow the check-in prompts for each passenger.
3. Save a mobile boarding pass, print at home, or use an airport kiosk.

Arrive early on day of travel for bag drop and security. If check-in is blocked or your name doesn’t match your travel documents, contact Southwest support before you leave for the airport.

messages.content: Can I change my assigned seat?

Yes — all Southwest flights now feature assigned seating, and you can usually change seats after booking.

1. Go to Manage Reservation on Southwest.com or in the app.
2. Select your trip and choose Seats.
3. Pick available seats for each passenger and save.

Seat options and any fees depend on your fare (Wanna Get Away®, Wanna Get Away Plus®, Anytime, or Business Select®). If you need accessible seating, start with Disability-Related Accommodations before travel day.
